cap_or_unstated_claims.denominator_provenance: The fetched Marketplace universe was capped to the top 100 extensions by installs before the 87 executable and 7 dependency counts.
cap_or_unstated_claims.exact_claim: **Motivating measurement (§1.2.1, VS Code).** The extension host cannot unload an individual extension's code. Of the top-100 extensions by installs (Marketplace data retrieved June 9, 2026), **87 contain executable code** and therefore require a host restart on removal. `deactivate` is only a graceful-shutdown hook, and it **separates effect disposal from effect creation, violating locality of concern**. Only **7 of the top 100** declare `extensionDependencies` on a non-built-in extension, and `vscode.extensions.getExtension(...).exports` is typed `any` — so there is no checked interface between extensions.
cap_or_unstated_claims.load_bearing_decision_or_verdict: Whether Cordis-style unload/dependency machinery is justified for extension ecosystems generally.

cap_or_unstated_claims.denominator_provenance: Two named real stacks -> first 64 name-sorted ARWs from each -> accepted worker/queue arms -> reported saturation and retention verdict.
cap_or_unstated_claims.exact_claim: **Verdict: D13 is FALSE, and the queue is a measured negative result.** On two real 64-frame stacks, the pyramid fold's first doubling below 1.10x is 8→16: **1.082x** on `112MSDCF` and **1.078x** on `bee-3-cpl`. Decode saturates at 16 threads; fold saturates one doubling earlier, at eight workers. A bounded decode→fold rendezvous was implemented and proved byte-identical, but its best-of-five wall time was **1.3% slower** and **2.1% slower** on the two stacks. It therefore failed the preregistered 1.05x retention bar and was removed rather than shipped behind a flag.
cap_or_unstated_claims.load_bearing_decision_or_verdict: D13 FALSE, fold saturation at eight workers, and rejection of the bounded decode-fold queue.

cap_or_unstated_claims.denominator_provenance: 299-frame stack -> 75 sampled frames -> sensels pinned at least once -> f over sampled frames; the merge instead has an unknown per-pixel contributing set.
cap_or_unstated_claims.exact_claim: ORCH's fourth hypothesis -- the merge averaging clipped with unclipped frames -- is the one specific to strehl, and it is **supported**. Read-only, 75 of 299 frames of `dry-erase-marker-head-cpl`, green sensels only.  **Definition.** `f` = fraction of sampled frames in which a green sensel is pinned at `CONTAINER_MAX_DN`, over the 848,807 sensels pinned in at least one frame (**10.31 %** of the green plane).  | | count | share | |---|---|---| | `f == 1` -- pinned in **every** frame | 178,402 | **21.02 %** | | `0 < f < 1` -- pinned in **some** | 670,405 | **78.98 %** | B15 predicted in advance that if H-merge were the whole story, the `f == 1` share would be **comparable to the ~74.7 % of the defect the clip cleared**.  **Measured 21.02 % against a predicted ~74.7 %.** That is not a near miss and it is in the wrong direction. By the criterion I registered before looking, H-merge is therefore **a mechanism, not the only mechanism** -- the weaker claim.  **The most likely reason is a denominator error of mine**, and it is a real limitation rather than a rescue: I computed `f` over *all* sampled frames, but the merge is focus-gated and averages `n_eff` ~ 55 **contributing** frames per pixel, not 299. The frames contributing to a pixel are the ones in focus there, which are plausibly the ones where a specular highlight is pinned. `f` over the correct denominator would be **higher** than 0.6464. I have not measured it, because doing so needs the gate's per-pixel frame set, and I am not going to assert a number I did not compute.
cap_or_unstated_claims.load_bearing_decision_or_verdict: H-merge is a mechanism rather than the only mechanism under the registered 21.02% versus 74.7% bar.
cap_or_unstated_claims.missing_input: Export the gate's per-pixel contributing-frame set and recompute f over that set for all 299 frames.
cap_or_unstated_claims.true_population: The capture has 299 frames; the relevant true denominator is each pixel's actual focus-gated contributing-frame set.

cap_or_unstated_claims.denominator_provenance: 119MSDCF and 113MSDCF -> first 22 frames via --limit -> post-hoc N-matched comparison with complete 22-frame 109MSDCF.
cap_or_unstated_claims.exact_claim: `--limit 22` to match `109`'s frame count:  **Fact 15 (MEASURED, POST-HOC — not pre-registered).** At matched N = 22, CPL-off only:  | stack | ISO | `P(win_R ≠ win_W)` | `rho_W` @4.0 | `rho_X′` @4.0 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `119MSDCF` | 50 | 24.16% | 1.0838 | 1.1638 | | `109MSDCF` | 160 | 28.56% | 1.0827 | 1.1795 | | `113MSDCF` | 500 | 36.58% | 1.0612 | 1.0543 |  **The index-map disagreement rises monotonically with ISO — 24.16% → 28.56% → 36.58% over a 10× ISO range — and `rho_W` does not move at all (1.0838, 1.0827, 1.0612).** This is the sharpest form of fact 12: raising the sensor noise degrades the *winner index map* exactly as a winner's-curse account of the argmax predicts, and leaves the *acceptance set* untouched.  It also shows the apparent ISO trend in the full-N table (1.1076 / 1.0827 / 1.1793) was **N**, not ISO: `113MSDCF`'s `rho_W` falls from 1.1793 at N = 63 to 1.0612 at N = 22.  **Refused.** `--limit 22` truncates a 63-frame through-focus sweep rather than decimating it, so the N-matched `113` arm covers less focus depth than the full stack. I therefore report fact 15 as a **probe that removes one confound and introduces another**, and I do not claim a clean ISO-independence result. Three points on one body is not an ISO curve.
cap_or_unstated_claims.load_bearing_decision_or_verdict: The apparent monotone disagreement-with-ISO trend and ISO-independence interpretation.
cap_or_unstated_claims.missing_input: Use focus-range-matched decimation or complete stacks at controlled N/ISO instead of first-22 truncation.

cap_or_unstated_claims.denominator_provenance: 65/61/60-frame exposure stacks -> first 60 frames for matched-N arms -> blockwise M8-O rates; complete full-N arms are reported beside them.
cap_or_unstated_claims.exact_claim: | exposure | full-N M8-O | matched-N=60 M8-O | |---|---:|---:| | clean, 6 s | **4.333602%** | **4.460053%** | | middle, 2.5 s | **0.060236%** | **0.059903%** | | noisy, 1 s | **0.030963%** | **0.030963%** |  These are the preregistered 256-pixel-inset rates. Every noise-falsification condition fails in both ladders:  * ordering runs in the opposite direction; * noisy minus clean is `-4.302639` points full-N and `-4.429090` points at matched N; * noisy/clean is `0.007145x` and `0.006942x`; * `0/64` blocks have a higher noisy than clean rate.  Equalizing frame count does not change the conclusion. This experiment does **not** show M8-O rewarding photon noise in the registered direction. It does show a much larger exposure/output-range confound: the clean arm's high-rail clamp dominates the census. These three stacks therefore cannot license a general claim of noise invariance.
cap_or_unstated_claims.load_bearing_decision_or_verdict: The registered noise-rise trend was not observed after equalizing frame count.
cap_or_unstated_claims.true_population: Clean/middle/noisy stacks contain 65, 61, and 60 frames; the report also evaluates those complete populations.

notes: Every assigned candidate has one disposition and every assigned file has one complete-file attestation.
No candidate was classified unstated: where a load-bearing denominator remained unknown (M109), an outer 75-of-299 frame cap was already established and therefore controls the classification.
The top-100 extension claim was found by complete-file review but has no scanner occurrence; it is included as a scanner-missed cap claim without affecting candidate totals.

plausible_verdict_flips.why_plausible: The complete stacks are 79 and 299 frames, so fold depth, memory pressure, and queue overlap differ materially from the first-64 workload; the D13 or retention bar could move.
Every-second/every-third sampling necessarily misses adjacent-frame variation; the source already labels jitter a lower bound, so magnitude-sensitive design conclusions can strengthen or shift.

The registered 21.02% versus 74.7% quantitative bar was evaluated on all sampled frames, not each pixel's focus-gated contributors; the source says the correct f would be higher and leaves it unmeasured.
The SURVIVE boundary is 10%; reported cells include 10.12% and 9.03%, so an exhaustive pixel census can cross a categorical bar even though 30,000 seeded draws are substantial.

The five-frame input hull is explicitly an upper-bound instrument; the report later retracts its original link-2 verdict after correcting the mask, and a full 205-frame hull can further reduce claimed excursions.
Thirteen selected frames still cannot prove that no one of the other 192 frames spans a reported excursion or changes the monotone-envelope comparison.

The winning frame is the cap endpoint, a direct truncation warning. Later full-299-frame M87 evidence measures severe hair-tip loss, so the favorable bee halo cell is already superseded as a promotion signal even though M126's denominator gap remains open.
One frame and selected flat regions cannot establish cross-frame calibration stability; a multi-frame exhaustive region census could move the reported 1.00-1.07x margin around the shipped constant.
